summary: demo-awesome-date-parser-test exfiltrates form input and injects remote scripts behind a date-parser API
details: src/index.js is a heavily obfuscated (obfuscator.io string-array + RC4-style base64 decoder) single-file module whose exported demoParseDate function performs behavior unrelated to date parsing. On invocation it installs a jQuery click handler that reads input[name=name|age|address] from the host page, base64-encodes the values, stores them in localStorage under sendToUnload_secretDataForm / sendToUnload_secretDataBase64, and issues a fetch GET to a host derived from a page meta[demo-tag] element with the field values placed in the query string. A beforeunload listener then flushes the stashed values via two navigator.sendBeacon calls to the same remote host. The same code path calls injectScriptIfNeeded, which appends <script src="{HOST}/tag_added_via_script_file_tag_appending.js"> to <head> and evals a snippet loading {HOST}/tag_added_via_script_import.js, giving the remote host arbitrary JavaScript execution in the consumer's page. The obfuscated string array contains self-describing tokens including 'stolen-data-sended-on-unload-event' and 'stolenData send'. An embedded ~98KB base64 blob is decoded to a Uint8Array and offered as a file download via an <a download> element.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
